clue.text: View one teetotaller held — maintain the same position

indicators.note: held means the view word grips the other pieces within it

parts.note: a view is a sight
one is the Roman numeral I
TT is the abbreviation for a teetotaller

explanation.surface: Someone holding a view while sober refuses to budge from it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay put and not move or change your stance is the idiom meaning stay where you are.

clue.text: Careless fielders keep dropping Lancashire's opener

parts.note: slips are fielding positions beside the wicketkeeper in cricket

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of, so a letter is removed from the keep word

parts.note: to hold is to keep

indicators.note: opener means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Sloppy cricket fielders drop a catch off Lancashire's opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the slips are fielders standing next to the wicketkeeper; Lancashire is a county side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy and careless work is described with this synonym for untidy.

clue.text: Greek character telephones, initially, before he volunteers

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
..., the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A Greek man rings round before signing up as a volunteer.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer army.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth letter of the Greek alphabet is a character of that alphabet.

clue.text: Little interest shown by girl, actually

parts.note: int is the short form of interest
Ruth is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl shows only slight interest, actually.
explanation.definitionFit: Really or in fact is the adverbial phrase meaning actually.

clue.text: Overworked horse in roughly built hut with no roof

indicators.note: with no roof in a down entry means the top letter is removed

parts.note: a shack is a crude, roughly built hut

explanation.surface: A tired horse is kept in a crumbling roofless shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired or worn-out riding horse is an old sense of this word.

clue.text: A lake-like expansion of a river overseas

parts.note: a broad is a wide stretch of river forming a lake, as in the Norfolk Broads

explanation.surface: A geographical description of a river widening into a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are a region of eastern England whose wide, lake-like stretches of river are each called a broad.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a foreign country, away from home, is a synonym for being overseas.

clue.text: A rum graduate, eccentric one

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
a card is an eccentric or comic person
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A strange graduate is described as an odd one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the adjective odd, matching 'eccentric'; here it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This brand name is a well-known make of white rum, an example.

clue.text: Nearly caught in open, suddenly

indicators.note: caught in means held inside the open word

parts.note: overt means open, done publicly
nigh means nearly

explanation.surface: Almost caught out in the open without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening very quickly, as if in a single night, is the sense meaning suddenly.

clue.text: County Durham's top store wrecked

indicators.note: top in a down clue means the first letter of the word
wrecked means ruined, so the letters of the shop word are broken up

explanation.surface: A shop in County Durham has been destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges STORE to ORSET. Dorset is a county of south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the counties of England, an example of a county.

clue.text: The very same dialect in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of the words before it are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio programme uses exactly the same regional speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scatters the nine letters of DIALECT and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Things exactly alike in every way are synonymously described as the very same.

clue.text: Printer's machine — vandalised it openly

indicators.note: vandalised means smashed up, so the letters of the words that follow are broken apart

explanation.surface: A printing press was smashed up in broad daylight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vandalised' rearranges the eight letters of IT OPENLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot-metal typesetting machine that casts lines of type is this printer's device.

clue.text: Fine the Parisian in vehicle

indicators.note: in places the French article inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
le is the French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A traffic fine handed to a Parisian sitting in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine weather is clear weather, a synonym for bright and cloudless.

clue.text: A sculpted figure of Ulysses originally sited in Maine, perhaps

indicators.note: sited in means placed within, so the initial goes inside the state word

parts.note: Maine is one example of a US state

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the name it follows

explanation.surface: A sculpture of Ulysses Grant, perhaps, set up in Maine.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved or cast figure of a person is a statue, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cast a spell on the way in

definitions.meaning: a verb, to enchant or bewitch, stressed on the second syllable
a noun, the door or gate through which one enters

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means bewitch; as a noun it means a doorway, two senses of one spelling.

clue.text: Put off drinking tin or bottle

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the put off word swallows the tin word

parts.note: to deter is to put off
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Discouraged from drinking a can or a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass vessel into which wine is poured is a kind of bottle.

clue.text: Very poor organist shone, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of the two words come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A poorly paid church organist nonetheless played brilliantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges ORGANIST and SHONE, thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Living with very little money is the idiom for being very poor.

clue.text: One practising self-denial in a British town? Almost right

indicators.note: almost means the town name loses its last letter

parts.note: Staines is a town on the Thames in Surrey

explanation.surface: Someone living a self-denying life in an English town, nearly correct?
explanation.walkthrough: Staines is a town in Surrey, west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refrains from drink or indulgence is one practising self-denial.

clue.text: Note making one irritable? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: crotchety means irritable

explanation.surface: A message that puts someone in a bad mood, nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a written message; it is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter note in music is a type of note, an example.

clue.text: Amateur covering canvas with newspaper and rope?

parts.note: a Sunday is a weekend newspaper, as in the Sunday papers
a painter is the rope attached to the bow of a boat for tying it up

explanation.surface: An amateur artist uses newspaper and rope to protect a canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering canvas' belongs to the definition, describing someone who paints, not a cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobbyist who paints pictures at weekends is the phrase for an amateur artist.

clue.text: Dash over to look at Kirov's latest dancer

indicators.note: over means turned back, so the dash word is reversed

parts.note: to run is to dash
to eye is to look at

indicators.note: latest means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Hurry along to watch the newest performer of the Kirov Ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: Rudolf Nureyev danced with the Kirov Ballet before defecting to the West.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous Russian ballet star is an example of a dancer.

clue.text: People in costume

parts.note: a habit is a costume, such as a nun's or a riding habit

explanation.surface: People dressed up in costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to populate.
explanation.definitionFit: To live in a place, filling it with residents, is to people it.

clue.text: Sounds like outlawed Italian criminal

indicators.note: sounds like signals the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: banned means outlawed
It is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A gangster outlawed from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw or robber is a criminal, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Speed of an amateur penning short review

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the review word sits inside

parts.note: lay means non-professional, as in a lay person
crit is an informal shortening of critique, a review

explanation.surface: How fast an amateur writes a brief review.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisk eagerness and quickness of action is the sense in which this word means speed.

clue.text: Guy almost rented a small cabin

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a guy is a chap
let means rented out

explanation.surface: A man has nearly rented a small holiday cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden hut of the Swiss kind, used as a holiday cabin, is this type of small house.

clue.text: Ordinary people from Italy, loosely

indicators.note: loosely means not held in place, so the country's letters slip into another order

explanation.surface: Common folk from Italy, roughly speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-clergy members of a church are ordinary people, as opposed to priests.

clue.text: Plans to circulate junk mail

indicators.note: to circulate here means to go round, so the plans word is turned back

parts.note: maps are plans

explanation.surface: Plans to send round unwanted advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsolicited email advertising is called by this name, a synonym for junk mail.

clue.text: Beau's extremes of depravity?

indicators.note: extremes of points at the two end letters of the following word, read as a phrase joined by and

parts.note: the word whose first and last letters are taken, giving the answer

explanation.surface: Asking whether a lover's ways are the height of wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beau's' stands for 'Beau is'. The ends of 'depravity' are D and Y; say them as a phrase and you have a word for a beau, a man devoted to fine clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is an old word for a fop or man devoted to fine clothes, a synonym.

clue.text: Get out again and enjoy hanging around bar

indicators.note: hanging around means surrounding, so the enjoy word wraps the bar word

parts.note: to relish is to enjoy
a pub is a bar

explanation.surface: Someone gets out again to enjoy loitering near a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring out a book or edition once more is to issue it again; get out means publish.

clue.text: Boom crossing Plymouth river

indicators.note: crossing means spanning the two words, so the letters straddle the gap between them

explanation.surface: A floating barrier stretched across a river at Plymouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boom' looks like a noun for a river barrier; it is the verb, to prosper.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish and prosper is synonymous with business booming.

clue.text: Article given to yours truly — your old stone, a precious stone

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
thy is the old form of your
st is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: Someone is handed a stone of yours, a valuable gem.
explanation.definitionFit: The violet variety of quartz is classed as a precious or semi-precious gemstone.
